summary: The Justice for Ukrainian Children Act aims to address the unlawful transfer, deportation, indoctrination, and militarization of Ukrainian children by the Russian Federation. It authorizes funding from fiscal years 2027 through 2032 to investigate, document, and preserve evidence of these actions, locate and rehabilitate affected children, impose sanctions on individuals involved, and boost media programming to counter Russian disinformation.

affected_groups.effect: Individuals under 18 born or living in Ukraine who were forcibly transferred, deported, or indoctrinated may be targeted for rescue, tracking, and rehabilitation efforts supported by authorized U.S. funding.

Individuals found to have knowingly directed, participated in, or facilitated the unlawful transfer, deportation, indoctrination, or militarization of Ukrainian children are subject to U.S. property-blocking sanctions and visa revocations or denials.
affected_groups.group: Foreign persons involved in the transfer or deportation of Ukrainian children

affected_groups.effect: These entities receive authorization for increased funding and surge programming to expand broadcast capacity and jamming circumvention in targeted regions.
affected_groups.group: Broadcasting entities (Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty and Voice of America)

key_provisions: Requires the U.S. Permanent Representative to the United Nations to veto UN Security Council resolutions that absolve Russia of accountability regarding Ukrainian children.

Authorizes at least $15,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2032 from National Security Investment Programs to collect evidence, operate a centralized database, and rescue and rehabilitate abducted children.
Mandates formal agreements and security protocols between the Secretary of State, civil society organizations, and the Ukrainian Ministry of Justice before database funds can be spent.
Requires the Secretary of State to submit annual reports to Congress regarding fund usage, database status, and actions taken to prioritize the return of deported children.

Requires the President to impose property blocking and visa bans on any foreign person who knowingly directs, participates in, or facilitates the unlawful transfer or indoctrination of Ukrainian children.

Authorizes at least $10,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2032 for surge programming in specific language services of Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty and Voice of America to combat disinformation.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Justice for Ukrainian Children Act aims to address the unlawful transfer, deportation, indoctrination, and militarization of Ukrainian children by the Russian Federation. It authorizes funding from fiscal years 2027 through 2032 to investigate, document, and preserve evidence of these actions, locate and rehabilitate affected children, impose sanctions on individuals involved, and boost media programming to counter Russian disinformation.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a multi-year financial and diplomatic commitment to counter Russian actions against Ukrainian children by combining targeted sanctions, evidence collection databases, support for rescue operations, and anti-disinformation broadcasting. It rates as a moderate-to-substantial legislative effort within foreign policy and international humanitarian accountability.
